title: My first game is playable, and releasing it on Steam is my next dream. I’d love your honest feedback.
author: abner-ruza
selftext:
Hey everyone!

Yesterday I released another game I’d been working on, and it was really well received. That gave me the confidence to share **CytoSquad** with you too.

CytoSquad is my first game, and making it has been a dream come true. There’s something surreal about seeing an idea turn into something people can actually play.

It’s an action survival roguelite set inside the human body. You control an immune cell fighting viruses, bacteria, and bosses, either solo or with up to 4 players in online co-op. I’m building it in Godot with AI assistance.

**The playable beta is available now for Windows** in itch io

I really want to bring it to Steam someday, but honestly, I’m afraid it’ll flop. I’m proud of how far I’ve come, but I’d love some outside perspective on what’s working and what still needs improvement.

* Does the concept catch your interest?
* If you try it, what feels fun, confusing, or frustrating?
* What would you want improved before a Steam release?

Honest criticism is welcome. Making my first game was a dream; now I want to learn how to make it better.

Thanks for taking a look!
